page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-16 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance based on the x86_64 architecture. It is equipped with 16 dedicated vCPUs, which are mapped to 8 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor, supporting 2 threads per core. The instance features 64 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include integrated GPU accelerators or local storage, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark evaluations, the AMD EPYC processor shows strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, ranking in the top 25%. Multi-core performance, including stress-ng multi-core and Passmark CPU scores, falls into the average tier. Memory bandwidth is stable, with cached small-block reads at 1013.33 GB/sec and uncached large-block reads at 93.7 GB/sec. For specialized workloads, the instance demonstrates strong text generation speeds of 277.2 tokens per second during LLM inference with a small 135M model, while medium 7B model inference and database operations remain in the average tier.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the n2d-standard-16 offers a balanced resource density suitable for mainstream enterprise workloads without the premium cost of memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated hardware. The absence of local NVMe storage means storage-heavy workloads must rely on external network-attached volumes, which is a key architectural tradeoff. This instance is well-suited for general-purpose applications, including static web serving, software compilation, medium-scale database operations, and moderate LLM inference tasks.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-16 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance featuring 16 dedicated vCPUs and 64 GB of RAM, powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor with x86_64 architecture. It provides a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, with 8 physical cores and 2 threads per core. The instance does not include bundled local storage or GPU accelerators. In benchmark evaluations, it demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance and strong text generation speeds for small LLM inference models, while multi-core compute, memory bandwidth, and database operations perform in the average tier. This resource profile offers a cost-effective balance for general-purpose workloads. It is highly suitable for static web serving, software compilation, and moderate database operations that do not require high-speed local NVMe storage.
